Historical certificate file hash is mandatory. Publication requires exact historical shard hashes, config hashes, non-weight hashes, counts, plan binding and independently plan-derived index/byte mapping. Uniformly altered but internally consistent fake quantization is rejected.
Real telemetry remains visible. Existing paced resource reasons including HOLD are rejected; whole-stage swap baseline is retained through conversion, assembly, finalize and certification.
Maximum 750 unit attempts and 344 quantizations; no automatic retry of failed unit evidence.
limitations: No real MLX import, quantization, native kernel, cache reconstruction, model load, forward, backward or update was executed by this reviewer.

Real four-shard source files were checked for existence and exact byte sizes only. Their 17,534,339,512 payload bytes were not independently rehashed in this review; execution must retain the implemented full source SHA verification.
CPU MLX uses unified memory. RSS is sampled at operation boundaries, not a hard interruptible mid-operation ceiling; no claim of zero Metal allocator initialization is made.
A CPU/GPU or runtime quantization difference must stop on historical certificate mismatch; this review does not authorize replacing the historical identity target.
This verdict covers runtime preparation only and provides no inference, training or accuracy qualification.
